scope: Primary-source SQLite lifecycle design research and invented tiny process-crash counterexample; no production changes or scientific runs.

claims_used: BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts write transaction immediately and may yield SQLITE_BUSY
COMMIT can yield SQLITE_BUSY and leave transaction active
rollback-mode FULL is not necessarily power-loss durable
EXTRA adds directory sync after rollback journal unlink
transactions durable across application crashes irrespective of sync/journal mode
atomic commit scope and hardware/filesystem assumptions
external arbitrary application files are outside SQLite transaction
rollback-journal locking and hot-journal process/OS/power-loss recovery

own_artifacts.result: PASS; child exited 73 inside release transaction; external file remained, DB release row absent, dependent remained unresolved; exact replay committed once; test confirms an empty ready frontier can coexist with pending unresolved work.

non_claims: No OS crash, power cut, fsync fault, disk-full condition, corruption, or production queue code was exercised.
The SQLite documentation does not establish the deployed filesystem/storage behavior.
The evidence does not make separate JSON publication and SQLite commit one atomic operation.
